issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect Milkable.messageOnMilk() to be a parameterless method returning a String (per UML and example usage in Main), but the solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) with a double parameter and implements it accordingly in Goat and Seal. This parameter mismatch will cause confusion and compilation errors if students follow the template/Main usage or the problem specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to match the problem/template by removing the parameter — declare Milkable.messageOnMilk() : String and update Seal and Goat to implement the parameterless method returning "[AnimalType] [name] is milked". Alternatively, if a volume parameter is intended, update the problem statement, UML, template Main usage, and tests to expect messageOnMilk(double) and update example return text accordingly.

issues.description: The Milkable interface's method signature differs between the problem/template and the solution: the problem statement and the template's Main call expect messageOnMilk() with no parameters, while the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) and implementations in Seal and Goat accept a double. This mismatch prevents students from mapping the required no-argument messageOnMilk() behavior described in the exercise to the provided solution code and will cause compilation/runtime confusion when following the template's example usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable API consistent: change the solution to use messageOnMilk() with no parameters (String return) in Milkable and update Seal and Goat to implement messageOnMilk() returning "[AnimalType] [name] is milked". Alternatively, update the problem statement and template examples to require messageOnMilk(double volume) and document the volume parameter — but prefer the former to match the described UML and template usage.
